messages.content:
Risk: LLM Supply Chain
Description: LLM supply chains are susceptible to various vulnerabilities, which can affect the integrity of training data, models, and deployment platforms. These risks can result in biased outputs, security breaches, or system failures. While traditional software vulnerabilities focus on issues like code flaws and dependencies, in ML the risks also extend to third-party pre-trained models and data.
Concern: None
Policy: Supply Chain & Geopolitical Risks

Candidate ontology classes:
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/Documents/Specification: specification — explicit requirement or set of requirements to be satisfied by something, such as a product, material, model, process or system [found by 8/13 queries]
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#HealthDataExposure: Health Data Exposure — Unauthorized disclosure of protected health information including medical records, diagnoses, treatments, or prescription histories. [found by 7/13 queries]
  Siblings: Unauthorized Surveillance, Direct Identifier Exposure, Employment Data Exposure
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/Documents/Reference: reference — source that may be used to ascertain, interpret, or understand something [found by 7/13 queries]
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#FinancialDataExposure: Financial Data Exposure — Disclosure of personal financial information including account numbers, credit scores, or transaction histories without authorization. [found by 7/13 queries]
  Siblings: Unauthorized Surveillance, Health Data Exposure, Direct Identifier Exposure
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/RegulatoryAgencies/RegulatoryReport: regulatory report — document required to support operational transparency that demonstrates compliance with some specification, law, policy, restriction, or other rule specified by a regulatory agency [found by 7/13 queries]
  Siblings: technical specification document, registry, transaction record

axes.rationale: The risk involves vulnerabilities in the integrity of models and processes within the supply chain. Specifications define the requirements for these components, and deviations from them represent the core of the supply chain risk.

Regulatory reports and compliance documentation are the instruments used to audit and verify the integrity of the supply chain, making them a key dimension for exploring how risks are detected or obscured.
